A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TabDPT research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across layout changes.

before.justification: V2 reports original classification and regression experiments, SSL and retrieval ablations, scaling experiments, few-shot results and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and reports additional baseline comparisons, a training-only TabDPT control and critical-difference analyses.

M1.justification: The transformer architecture, SSL augmentations, retrieval procedures, classification encoding, PCA and few-shot pseudo-labeling remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 and Appendices C–D match substantively; expanded descriptions do not establish an algorithmic revision.

E1.justification: The 123 pre-training datasets, 107 CC18/CTR23 evaluation datasets and seven few-shot datasets are retained. V3 additionally summarizes external TabArena evaluations, but supplies no dataset inventory establishing whether they introduce distinct data coverage or reuse overlapping datasets.

E2.justification: V3 adds TabM to the CC18/CTR23 comparisons. Vanilla TabPFN, already present in v2's IQM Table F.1, appears in v3's Table 1 and is added to the dataset-stratified comparisons in Figures F.1–F.3. The other principal baselines remain.

E3.justification: Table 1 changes from average ranks to average metric scores, and v3 adds a training-only TabDPT control excluding validation examples. Figure 4 also reports a convergence check extending to 1,024 epochs. Default TabDPT's use of combined training and validation data is newly disclosed, rather than established as a change to existing runs.

E4.justification: The new no-validation control examines the benefit of additional labeled context. Figure 4 newly reports a longer-training saturation check, and Figures F.1–F.3 extend existing dataset-characteristic analyses with additional comparators. The original SSL/retrieval ablations and Appendix A findings remain.

E5.justification: New Appendix G adds critical-difference analyses with multiple-hypothesis adjustments and distinguishes dataset-level uncertainty from suite-level bootstrap uncertainty. Bootstrapped 95% confidence intervals, at least two data splits and 50 few-shot seeds were already reported; no increase in repeated-run counts is stated.

E6.justification: The numerical summaries are substantially revised: v2 Table 1 reports TabDPT's CC18 accuracy rank as 2.833, whereas v3 reports accuracy 0.884, alongside new no-validation and TabM results of 0.874 and 0.878. V2's separate IQM Table F.1 is removed. V3 also adds stratified, critical-difference, convergence and attributed TabArena findings. These changed summaries and settings do not establish a same-setting performance gain or loss.

T1.justification: The prediction equation, classification encoding argument and scaling-law formulation are retained. No new formal assumptions, theorems or proofs appear. The invariance discussion is explanatory, and the critical-difference analyses concern empirical statistics.

C1.justification: The central SSL, retrieval and scaling contributions remain. Section 1 narrows the real-versus-synthetic advantage to competing open-source generators and replaces Internet-scale aspirations with large-scale ones. It adds TabArena-specific claims of leading fully open-source TFMs and placing third overall.

C2.justification: V3 explains the validation-access imbalance and how to interpret the training-only comparison. It limits the stated significant advantage over TabPFN v2 to CC18 accuracy and acknowledges that tree pipelines can provide faster inference when training costs are excluded. It also expands the row/column invariance rationale; existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: V3 newly documents the absence of positional encoding, feature/class permutations for ensemble members and default merging of training and validation data. The architecture tables, optimizer settings, preprocessing, training pseudocode and code-resource link targets remain substantively unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds references to TabM, TabArena, TabPFN-2.5 and Li et al.'s semi-supervised ICL work, while removing Wen et al.'s From supervised to generative reference. It also acknowledges TabPFN v2's shared classification/regression architecture and adds external-leaderboard positioning.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites and explanatory paragraphs expand the introduction, methodology and experimental discussion. Appendix F.2 is removed and Appendix G added, while the main narrative sequence remains. Author order, correspondence information and the conference header are updated.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains revised columns, additional rows and underlining for the comparison excluding validation examples. Figures F.1–F.3 are redrawn with expanded legends and revised axes; the IQM table disappears and four critical-difference diagrams are added. Figure 3 moves, while the principal architecture, scaling and ablation graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 improves comparison fairness by disclosing validation-data access and adding training-only TabDPT and TabM results. Adjusted statistical comparisons and the inference-only speed qualification also improve interpretation. These gains outweigh the loss of the separate IQM table, although the relationship between the replacement score summaries and Appendix G's IQM/rank discussion remains unclear.
